summary: Ottawa National Forest fire tower, 100 ft Aermotor built by CCC Company 3611 in 1939-40; replaced by air detection in 1970.

events.note: Erected by CCC Company 3611 in 1939-40 per the register; a forest lookouts site gives 1940 as the completion year.
Remained active until 1970, when air detection replaced it, per the register.
Registered in the National Historic Lookout Register on May 30, 1996.

evidence.quote: Company 3611 (James Lake) of the Civilian Conservation Corps erected Gibbs Fire Tower in 1939-40.

evidence.supports: 100-ft Aermotor with 7 by 7 ft metal cab; active until 1970, then replaced by air detection
evidence.quote: The 100’ Aermotor tower with 7’x 7’ metal cab remained active until 1970 when it was replaced by air detection.

evidence.supports: Only remaining fire tower on the Iron River district of the Ottawa National Forest
evidence.quote: This is the only remaining fire tower on the Iron River district of Michigan’s Ottawa National Forest.

evidence.supports: Administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Completed in 1940 by members of Company 3611
evidence.quote: 1940: This 100-foot Aermotor tower was completed by members of Company 3611 of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

corrections.why: The register places the tower in Iron County, Michigan, at N 46.179955° W 088.698405°. The brief's point is in the Lower Peninsula, several hundred kilometres away.
Same register coordinates as the lat correction.
The register gives the elevation as 1,683 ft (513 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says erected 1939-40; the forest lookouts site says completed 1940. Both fit, so the story gives the register's range and notes 1940 as completion.

notes_for_editor: Current condition and access are not described by any source found, so the story says so. Brief coordinates and elevation were wrong (see corrections). The brief's 'unknown' status is left unresolved. The SAH Archipedia Camp Gibbs page returned 403 and was not read.
